documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements - Six months ended 30 June 2026
Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Cargills Bank PLC, a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). Single-entity filing -- no separate Group/Company columns anywhere in this filing (no subsidiaries listed in corporate information), so entered as a single basis='GROUP' row per this project's convention for single-entity bank/NBFI filings. This entry uses the 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) figures, consistent with how SAMP was entered this session; the filing also separately provides quarter-only columns (not used here). Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (Net interest income + Net fees and commission income + Total other income); operating_profit = 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services', the Bank's own subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- interest expense is already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income. 'Taxes on financial services' (Rs.275,789k for H1 2026) is not a separate stored field -- profit_before_tax stored here is AFTER this levy, matching the filing's own 'Profit before tax' line. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, loans & advances is the core lending book not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks' (genuine interbank borrowing); long_term_borrowings = 'Due to other borrowers'. 'Due to depositors' (Rs.77,855,724k) is deliberately excluded -- deposit funding, not debt. shares_in_issue = 1,239,842,858 (period-end count, per the shareholder-information page and confirmed via Net Assets Value per share: 14,642,063k/11.81=1,239,802,963, matching). Note: the Bank completed a Rs.2.5bn Rights Issue during the period (294.2mn new shares, listed 9 April 2026), so period-end shares_in_issue is materially higher than the weighted-average share count implied by the disclosed EPS of 0.16 -- this is expected and not a data error (EPS uses time-weighted shares over the period, not the period-end count). No column-swap issues found -- P&L, balance sheet, and segmental note all reconcile internally.

interim_updates.note_text: Cargills Bank's Total Operating Income was roughly flat YoY (+0.9% to Rs.2.78bn) for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), but PBT fell 21.9% to Rs.362.4mn (from Rs.464.1mn) and PAT fell 24.8% to Rs.180.7mn (from Rs.240.4mn). By segment, the Banking segment (core lending/deposit business) swung from a Rs.27.3mn LOSS to a Rs.306.0mn PROFIT before tax, driven by a 42% increase in segment net interest income to Rs.2,055mn -- a genuine, strong core-business improvement. This was more than offset by the Treasury and Investments segment, whose PBT fell 88.5% to Rs.56.5mn (from Rs.491.3mn), as the filing explains: lower realised capital gains on the derecognition of financial assets and reduced net gains from FVTPL financial assets, against an unusually high comparative-period base (2025 had benefited from a large one-off gain). Net Interest Income grew 20.2% YoY to Rs.2,207mn as Net Interest Margin improved to 4.64% from 4.38% (year-end 2025 reference), and Net Fee & Commission Income grew 17.3% on deposit, credit card and trade-finance fee growth. The Bank's asset quality improved: total impairment charge fell 44.6% to Rs.99.7mn (from Rs.180.1mn), and the Gross Stage 3 (impaired-loan) ratio dropped to 11.30% from 12.00% at year-end 2025. Total operating expenses grew 11.3% YoY (Personnel expenses +16.6% on salary increments; Depreciation & amortisation +34.9% on IT/infrastructure investment), pushing the Cost-to-Income Ratio to 73.43% from 70.68% at year-end 2025. Earlier in the year the Bank raised Rs.2.5bn of equity capital via a Rights Issue (294.2mn new shares, listed 9 April 2026) to meet a Central Bank directive to strengthen its capital base and reduce major shareholders' combined stake toward 50% -- this is why period-end shares in issue (1,239.8mn) diluted EPS materially versus the prior year (Rs.0.16 vs Rs.0.28, -42.9%, a steeper decline than the 24.8% PAT decline alone would suggest).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for CBNK -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol (indeed the first document of any kind collected for this ticker in this database). This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1) figures rather than a discrete quarter, since Cargills Bank has a 31 December FYE and reports this way; the filing's own quarter-only columns (also available) were not used, to keep this entry's period type consistent with other bank entries this session (e.g. SAMP).
interim_updates.takeaway: The core Banking segment's turnaround (from a Rs.27.3mn loss to a Rs.306.0mn profit, on 42% NII growth and materially lower impairment charges) is genuinely strong and reflects real credit-quality and margin improvement. The headline PBT/PAT decline is not a core-business problem -- it is the Treasury and Investments segment normalising after an unusually large capital-gains quarter a year earlier, plus EPS dilution from the Rights Issue completed to meet a Central Bank capital directive.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income roughly flat YoY (+0.9% to Rs.2.78bn); PBT -21.9% to Rs.362.4mn; PAT -24.8% to Rs.180.7mn
Banking segment PBT swung from a Rs.27.3mn loss to a Rs.306.0mn profit, driven by segment net interest income +42% to Rs.2,055mn -- the core driver of underlying improvement
Treasury and Investments segment PBT fell 88.5% to Rs.56.5mn (from Rs.491.3mn) as realised capital gains and FVTPL gains normalised off an unusually high 2025 comparative base
Total impairment charge fell 44.6% to Rs.99.7mn; Gross Stage 3 (impaired loan) ratio improved to 11.30% from 12.00% at year-end 2025 -- genuine asset-quality improvement
Net loan book grew 15% (Rs.9.2bn) since December 2025 to Rs.72.3bn (+28% YoY); customer deposits grew 18% to Rs.77.9bn (+32% YoY)

Rs.2.5bn equity Rights Issue completed (294.2mn new shares, listed 9 April 2026) per a Central Bank directive to strengthen capital and reduce major shareholders' combined stake toward 50% by 2029 -- diluted EPS to Rs.0.16 from Rs.0.28 (-42.9%, steeper than the PAT decline alone)
key_drivers: Banking segment net interest income +42% YoY (Rs.1,449mn to Rs.2,055mn per the segmental note) is the primary driver of the segment's swing from loss to profit -- a genuine core-business improvement

Treasury and Investments segment PBT -88.5% YoY is explicitly attributed by the Bank to lower realised capital gains on derecognition of financial assets and reduced FVTPL gains, against an unusually strong prior-year comparative -- not an operating weakness
Total impairment charge -44.6% YoY (Rs.180.1mn to Rs.99.7mn) reflects genuine asset-quality improvement (Gross Stage 3 ratio down to 11.30% from 12.00%), not just lower provisioning discipline

The Rights Issue (294.2mn new shares) mechanically dilutes EPS regardless of profit trend -- period-end shares in issue (1,239.8mn) are ~31% higher than the ~945.6mn shares outstanding at 31 December 2025
